body.statement: Theorem 1 (effect-specific rational-positive separation). For every finite input \(\mathfrak u\) accepted by \(\mathrm{def{:}certified\text{-}input}\), every \(D\in\mathfrak D\), and every outcome cell \(y\), if \(F_{D,y}\notin K_{\mathcal I}\), then there exists \(p^{\dagger}\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\cap\mathbb Q^{\Omega}\) whose reduced coordinate numerators and denominators have bit length at most \(B_{\mathrm{cert}}\) such that \(F_{D,y}(p^{\dagger})\ne0\). Conversely, \(F_{D,y}\in K_{\mathcal I}\) implies \(T_{D,y}(p)=T_{D_0,y}(p)\) for every \(p\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\).

obligation.what_is_open: Show that every intervention signature outside the saturated real-radical ideal is nonzero at a strictly positive rational table satisfying all bit-one equalities and all bit-zero inequalities, with coordinate height at most the declared certificate bound.
obligation.obstruction: Real-radical nonmembership can be witnessed on an equality component disjoint from the positive exact-oracle chamber containing the supplied rational feasibility point. Saturation excludes zero factors but neither selects signs nor guarantees a rational point on the separating component.
obligation.attempted: The real-variety evaluation argument proves the converse. Rational approximation fails because it need not preserve the conditional-independence equations. The new chart lemma gives a finite rational-grid separator whenever a rational open-box chart with nonzero pulled-back signature is available, but the frozen hypotheses do not supply such a chart on every detected component or the advertised global height bound.
obligation.partial_result: The membership-to-equality direction is completely proved by \(\mathrm{lem{:}equality\text{-}branch\text{-}soundness}\). In addition, \(\mathrm{lem{:}rational\text{-}grid\text{-}separator\text{-}on\text{-}chart}\) proves the constructive implication on any rational open-box chart whose pullback of \(F_{D,y}\) is nonzero: a grid of at most \((e+1)^k\) rational points contains a strictly positive rational exact-oracle separator. The remaining step is precisely to prove that such a chart exists for every \(F_{D,y}\notin K_{\mathcal I}\) and that its induced coordinate height is at most \(B_{\mathrm{cert}}\).

body.justification: This is the load-bearing bridge from an algebraic failed equality to a checkable statistical ambiguity table.
body.gap: Garcia, Stillman, and Sturmfels provide saturated components and effective algebra decides real feasibility, but neither yields a rational positive exact-oracle point separating a graph-indexed intervention signature.
body.consumer: A discovery package can certify nonidentification with a finite rational table that users can inspect and replay exactly.
